title: Borrowing money and buying a saxophone with Big Eye Louie
summary: He explains how Big Eye Louie told him of a pawned saxophone, and how he borrowed $60 and was third in New Orleans to buy one, after Lou Warnick and Sam Dutrey.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: So, Bob Lyons, he had a shoe black stand on Ramport and Perdita. Well, that's where all the positioners' headquarters was. When they'd get up in the daytime, they'd go around Bob Lyons and have their fun. So, Bob brings me up. Old Rivers, look. Say, I want you to come over here. I got something nice I want to tell you about. I was anxious to know this about it. Come over and say, listen. Say, Big Eye Louie come in town with a saxophone. C-Mell and a saxophone. And he says that he pawned it. Yeah. Well, I go and see about the saxophone. I'll see about the saxophone. Tell me. He says, yeah. He says, we want $60 for it. I didn't know anything about it. So, what I do, I go and grab me at Ramport at a saloon. Prior to it was Ben Mulligan. He's leaving me have anything. I say, Mr. Ben, I say, I'd like to borrow $60. That's all you want? Yes, $60. Because I returned back. That's all right. $60 that goes around on Camp Street at the Blueprint where Lou Warnick wait. You heard of Lou Warnick?
He used to play with Big Eye out at the Luchin's.
He used to play with Piron.
Yes. That's right. He was with that band. I saw him out at Big Eye one time at the Luchin's.
Not speaking about Big Eye Louie.
I know. But they weren't if you played sax out there, too, with him once.

Well, during that time, he was playing for Spanish folk every night with Piron. And he worked at his blueprint place on Camp Street. So what I loved, he was the first man bought a saxophone in the Orleans. Lou Warnick.
You mean much before what you're saying?
Years before what you're talking about.

And the second one bought a saxophone in the Orleans was Sam Dutri. All right. Well, I was the third one bought a saxophone. Well, I was out to Louie's wake at his 12 o'clock hour. Goes there. Louie. I said, I bought a saxophone. Yeah. I said, but I told a man I have the money for it, but I told him I'd be back to see it. I said, all right, I'll go along with you if I have time. Let's go look at it. He comes, look at the saxophone. He says, he wants $60 for it. Yeah. I said, I have the $60 I borrowed from Mr. Van Mulliken. I said, all right, we're going to get that on cheaper than that. Well, we go to the place. Man, here's a saxophone in the Orleans. The Lloyd takes it, run over it, you know, he could play it. The man was busy, waiting on the customer. The man goes, wait on the customer. The Lloyd takes the trill of keys on his sax, the three keys on top, twist them around from the pads. He didn't have to use them when he made his little execution. He didn't have to use them at all. So, twist them. Here comes the fella. Well, how did I get? He said, oh, you're a nice player. Oh, you're a nice player. How are you nice? Well, pretty good, but he said that he needs a little overhauling. He said, what's the trouble with it? He said, let me see. They got three keys on all the way. He bought nothing. He said, well, I tell you, my friend. He said, that's my friend. I can't play it. He says, but I know music when I hear it. He said, I sell instruments around you. I know who can play and who can't play. And he says, I think you're a great player. He said, you're the first one I heard play it. He said, well, what do you think about it? He said, well, I'll tell you, sir. About $10. We'll fix it up. Right. $50. Get to $50. All right. Come on, we got time. Let's go around the place. Going back around the place, can't speak. He said, you know you're going to be a better factor for Onclair. Than I am in a Clarinet player. Because of the way you play. You cut out for that. I said, oh, no, Lord. He said, I'm going to show you the scale on it. Show me the scale on it. I said, the Rams like to climb that. I just take the scale. See me at the scale. Up and down. All right. Thank you. Well, I takes it home. And I started working hard on it. Then, I was hired to play in the cabaret. Went out in the cabaret, a dreamland cabaret. And I'm going to play a clarinet and saxophone. Now, I spent about three years since I left Los Angeles.
